summary:
**Independent score: 9.0/10 for visual quality and the reviewed UI changes.** No blocking findings in the inspected source and representative native captures.

The charcoal surfaces, hierarchy, queue selection, artwork, and white controls closely follow the web reference. The inspected 480pt and 125% captures retain usable controls without visible horizontal overflow. Focus correctly shows a small thumbnail with no visible video.

Two minor refinements remain:

- **P3 — Desktop media proportions:** The desktop video sits farther inside the deck than in the reference, leaving broader shoulders. Consider widening it where viewport height permits. [NativeUIStyle.swift](/Users/gustavocaiano/.t3/worktrees/tubeshuffle/t3-310b873b/macos/TubeShuffle/App/NativeUIStyle.swift:151)
- **P3 — Shortcuts button prominence:** The full-width shortcuts button carries more visual weight than the reference’s centered compact action. Reduce its width if closer similarity is desired. [NativeLibraryView.swift](/Users/gustavocaiano/.t3/worktrees/tubeshuffle/t3-310b873b/macos/TubeShuffle/App/NativeLibraryView.swift:262)

Source inspection supports actual `WKWebView.isHidden`, stable representable identity, window-scoped zoom handling, sheet exclusion, and monitor cleanup. The keyboard monitor alongside menu commands has a clear purpose when WebKit owns focus; I found no actionable complexity objection.

This assessment uses source, static native captures, and synthetic test assertions. I did not independently rerun tests or validate live interaction. The pending full-suite/package result remains unconfirmed. Hidden playback, audio, OAuth, YouTube policy, and release acceptance remain unvalidated. No files changed.
